gloss: first working day of the new year

definitions.gloss: first working day of the new year; resumption of work after New Year
definitions.explanation: The day businesses and government offices reopen after the New Year holidays, usually January 4 in Japan. Also the small ceremonies held on that day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{仕事始|しごとはじ}めだ。
examples.english: Tomorrow is the first working day of the year.

examples.japanese: {仕事始|しごとはじ}め⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{年頭|ねんとう}→年頭：21721_nentou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: On the first working day, the president gave a New Year address.

examples.japanese: {仕事始|しごとはじ}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{同僚|どうりょう}→同僚：01023_douryou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{近|ちか}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦お{参|まい}り→お参り：16837_omairi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ことにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: On the first working day of the year, I make a point of visiting a nearby shrine with my colleagues.

notes:
The counterpart of ⟦{仕事納|しごとおさ}め→仕事納め：16213_shigotoosame⟧, the last working day of the year (usually December 28). Government offices follow the same schedule, and the day is often called {御用始|ごようはじ}め in official contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事始|しごとはじ}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: the first working day
- {仕事始|しごとはじ}め{式|しき}: a ceremony on the first working day

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many companies start the year with a short speech from the head of the company, and some staff visit a shrine together to pray for business success. Real work often starts only the next day.
